table.ruleA: Add charge-table units to each form; volume not enforced.
table.ruleB: Add ingest-schedule chunks to each tier; budget not enforced.

table.ruleA: Forms handled in order 1 to 6, one at a time. If contents are above volume (strictly), the excess goes to form n+1 and the form is set to its volume; form 6's excess goes to waste. Overflow reaches the next form before that form is handled.
table.ruleB: Tiers handled in order 1 to 6, one at a time. If count is above budget (strictly), the excess goes to tier n+1 and the tier is set to its budget; tier 6's excess is dropped. Eviction reaches the next tier before that tier is handled.

table.ruleA: Read contents after Step 2. GREEN at or above the upper mark becomes HOT; HOT at or below the lower mark becomes GREEN; otherwise no change; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle, form, before, after).
table.ruleB: Read count after eviction. COLD at or above the heat mark becomes HOT; HOT at or below the cool mark becomes COLD; otherwise no change; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle, tier, before, after).

table.ruleA: Amounts come from contents at the start of the step, using the status after Step 3: GREEN gives floor(contents/4), HOT gives floor(contents/2). All six are worked out first, then applied together. Each form loses its amount. GREEN amounts go to waste. HOT amounts go to form n-1, and form 1's HOT amount goes to waste. Volume is not enforced.
table.ruleB: Amounts come from the count at the start of the step, using the state after step 3: COLD gives floor(count/4), HOT gives floor(count/2). All six are worked out first, then applied together. Each tier loses its amount. COLD amounts are dropped. HOT amounts go to tier n-1, and tier 1's HOT amount is dropped. Budget is not enforced.

table.ruleA: Sum all six. If the total is MORE THAN 38 (strictly), every form becomes floor(contents/2), the removed units go to waste, and the cycle is logged. At exactly 38, nothing happens.
table.ruleB: Sum all six. If the total is 38 OR MORE, every tier becomes floor(count/2), the removed chunks are dropped, and the cycle is logged. At exactly 38, it fires.
table.difference: The trigger comparison differs. A uses total > 38 and B uses total >= 38, so a total of exactly 38 fires a reset in B but not in A. What is halved, what is kept, which positions are affected and where the removed units go are all the same.

table.ruleA: (a) End contents for forms 1-6, (b) end statuses, (c) all status changes, (d) washout cycles, (e) final waste tally, (f) balance check: start plus charges equals end plus waste.
table.ruleB: (a) End counts for tiers 1-6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes in the order they occurred, (d) reset cycles, (e) final drop count, (f) balance check showing both sides.
table.difference: Only the presentation differs: B asks for changes in occurrence order and for both sides of the balance to be shown. The content is the same.
